title: Coordinated graded-degradation and region warmup coordinator for stable autoscaling
creator: Kunal Rao
description:
Problem: During region failovers and sudden traffic spikes our current readiness/liveness signals are too binary which causes autoscaler thrashing and blunt failover behavior. This leads to repeated cold starts, increased p99 latency, and temporary SLO violations for multi-region customers.

Goal: Implement a coordinated "graded-degradation" controller plus a region warmup coordinator that smooths readiness signals, exposes degradation bands for circuit breakers, and sequences autoscaler handoffs to avoid oscillation while preserving SLOs. The solution must be compatible with Redwood's routing/fallback layer and the Dedicated/Private modes.

Scope:
- Define health-band states (GREEN/DEGRADED-1/DEGRADED-2/RED) derived from smoothed probe metrics, synthetic warmup transactions, and token-weighted latency percentiles.
- Implement Warmup Coordinator: a short-lived regional controller that pre-warms model caches, issues synthetic traffic, and only promotes instances to GREEN after a programmable warmup score.
- Graded Circuit Breaker: triggers progressive load shedding and route weighting changes based on band, with hysteresis windows to avoid flip-flopping.
- Autoscaler Handoff Policy: damped ramping when moving capacity responsibility between regions (precondition checks and handshake signals).
- Telemetry & Rollout: dashboards, alerts, and an experiment plan with canary rollout across low-traffic customers.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of autoscaler algorithm; wide changes to public customer APIs.

Links: design doc (drive) and prototype scripts are referenced below.
acceptance_criteria: New health-band state machine computed in runtime and visible in Console per-region for all traffic
Warmup coordinator reduces first-request p99 by >=30% in canary regions compared to baseline
Autoscaler handoffs show <10% request loss and <2x thrash during operated failover tests
No increase in steady-state token cost >2% for controlled workloads
Runbook updated and on-call playbooks include graded-degradation recovery steps
tasks: Define health-band scoring (metrics, weights, smoothing windows)
Prototype warmup coordinator service (k8s controller) and synthetic txn generator
Integrate health-band output into circuit-breaker routing layer
Implement autoscaler handoff API (promote/demote signals + cooldowns)
Add telemetry dashboards and SLO regression alerts
End-to-end chaos test: regional termination + traffic shift experiment
Write runbook and orchestrate canary rollout with SRE
test_plan: Local integration harness + staging canary. Steps: (1) Unit tests for health-band logic, (2) Integration with synthetic traffic in staging, (3) Run gradual failover test across 3 regions with 5k rps baseline, (4) Monitor SLOs and rollback if p99 > baseline*1.15.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy warmup coordinator to staging and enable for internal traffic; 2) Canary region A (1% of customers) for 48h; 3) Expand to up to 5% and run chaos tests; 4) If stable, ramp to all regions over 2 weeks with monitoring gates; rollback toggles available in Console.
